title: Acceptance spec for structured outputs, function-call streaming, and error handling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket captures the product acceptance criteria and test cases for structured output behavior and function/tool calling semantics. Goals: (1) define how models must emit structured data (JSON schemas, typed fields, required vs optional), (2) define streaming semantics for partial structured output and function invocation events, and (3) enumerate error modes and fallback policies so SDKs and Redwood runtime have deterministic behaviors for customers.
background: Customers require deterministic contract semantics when using structured output or function/tool calling. Past incidents: PROD-488 (mis-parsed function args when streaming truncated), and ENG-3129 (runtime fallback invoked too late). This spec aligns console docs, SDKs, runtime routing, and example test harnesses to a single source of truth.
scope: Schema-first structured output: support for schema validation of top-level objects returned by generation
Streaming of structured outputs: incremental JSON chunks plus a finalization marker/event
Function/tool calling semantics: single-call vs multi-call, explicit call tokens in stream, and post-call metadata
Error modes: transient (retryable), recoverable-with-fallback, and terminal (user-facing error)
Runtime fallback behavior: automatic fallbacks to safe model variants or non-tooling paths
Acceptance tests and example prompts to be added to the eval harness
out_of_scope: New SDK language bindings (only doc updates here)
Network-level retries between region failover (handled by infra roadmap)
acceptance_criteria: Schema conformance: For any request with a 'response_schema' payload, responses must validate against the specified JSON Schema. If streaming, every final assembled JSON object must validate. Test: harness validates 100% of recorded sessions.

Partial/streaming behavior: When streaming structured outputs, the server will emit 'chunk' events with stable ordering and an explicit 'stream_end' event. Consumers must be able to reconstruct the final JSON by concatenating ordered chunks and must receive a stream_end timestamp and final length. Test: SDK test reads 50k tokens across 500 streaming sessions with 0 reorders.

Function-call emission: Tool invocations must appear as an explicit function_call event in the response stream with fields: name, args (JSON), call_id. The runtime must not interpret plain text as a function call—function_call events are machine-specified. Test: recorded session contains function_call event for each call attempt.

Multi-call sequences: For flows that invoke multiple tools, call events must include call_id and parent_call_id for causal linking. Acceptance: the eval harness replays multi-call flows and validates parent/child linkage for 1,000 scenarios.

Error mode classification: The API will expose an 'error_mode' with values 'transient', 'recoverable', 'terminal' for failures during generation or tool invocation. SDKs use this to decide retry vs fallback vs surface error. Test: deliberately cause network timeouts and verify errors are labeled 'transient' and retried once per config.

Graceful degradation: If a tool is unavailable or returns a terminal error, runtime must follow the configured policy: fallback_to_model_variant | partial_response | abort. Acceptance: for each policy, behavior matches spec in 100% of test runs.

Atomicity guarantees: Function calls must be delivered at-least-once to the downstream tool; runtime will provide call_id and a deduplication window header. Test: simulate duplicates and verify tools see idempotent handling via call_id.

Security and authorization: Tool calls that require customer secrets must include an authorization scope. The API surface will expose to-host header hints; no secrets are carried in function_call args. Acceptance: security review signs off and a pen-test validates no secret leaks in 3 scenarios.

Backward compatibility: Old clients not using streaming or response_schema must continue to receive the previous plain-text generation behavior. Acceptance: compatibility test matrix (SDK v1.x, v2.x) passes.

Observability: Each structured-output/func-call event must emit telemetry: request_id, call_id (if present), schema_id (if present), latency_ms, and final_validation_result. Test: logs for 10,000 synthetic requests include expected telemetry fields.

Documentation: Console docs, SDK examples, and PRD must have concrete examples for (a) schema failure modes, (b) streaming reassembly, (c) call_id deduplication, and (d) fallback configs. Acceptance: docs reviewed and approved by DevRel and Security.
Performance: Enabling streaming + schema validation should not increase p50 latency by more than 15% under typical payloads. Acceptance: benchmark suite shows delta <=15% on production-like load.
E2E test harness: Add canonical test set of 120 prompts covering schema edge cases (nested arrays, optional fields, partial streams) and verify deterministic outcomes across runtime and SDK clients.

Client error propagation: If schema validation fails server-side, the API returns a structured validation_error with schema_path, reason, and sample_payload. Acceptance: SDK surfaces validation_error with mapped fields in 100% of runs.

Finalization idempotency: stream_end events include final_checksum (SHA256 hex) for reconstructed payloads; clients must be able to verify checksum to detect silent corruption. Acceptance: checksum verified in 100% of fuzz tests.
test_cases: TC-001: Simple schema success — request with response_schema (flat object). Assert final JSON validates and stream_end present.
TC-002: Streaming partial object split across chunks — assemble, validate, checksum matches.
TC-003: Tool unavailable with fallback policy 'fallback_to_model_variant' — confirm model variant response returned and tool_call error recorded.
TC-004: Deduplication — send the same call_id twice and ensure tool sees single effect via idempotency header.
TC-005: Schema mismatch — server returns validation_error; SDK surfaces error with schema_path and sample payload.
TC-006: Multi-tool sequence — two consecutive function_call events with parent_call_id chain; verify causal links and telemetry.
TC-007: Performance regression — measure p50 with schema validation enabled vs disabled; assert <=15% regression.
TC-008: Auth scope enforcement — tool requiring customer secret must fail if scope missing, return recoverable error with guidance.
TC-009: Streaming network hiccup — simulate transient dropped chunk and verify SDK retry/reconnect behavior preserves ordering and final checksum.
TC-010: Back-compat smoke — legacy client receives plain text response when no response_schema provided.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy schema validation + streaming events to 5% of hosted API traffic with a feature flag; run E2E harness for 72h. Phase 2: Expand to dedicated clusters with opt-in config for fallbacks; collect telemetry and update docs. Phase 3: Default enable for new API versions and announce migration guide for existing customers.
